steps: When a client refers new business to the firm, the automation automatically sends a thank-you note or small reward the same week, reinforcing the referral relationship without relying on someone remembering to do it during a busy stretch.

The referral partner manager can see exactly who's referring and how often, sharpening which relationships deserve extra attention, and consistently acknowledging referrals in a timely way keeps the behavior going, since clients and partners who feel genuinely appreciated for a referral are far more likely to send another one.
automations.manualProcess: Without this system, a referral partner manager manually pieces together information from different places, then has to relay it to everyone who needs it. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Market Volatility Client Reassurance Communication
automations.summary: During a significant market move, the automation automatically sends a pre-approved reassurance communication to clients explaining the context in…
steps: During a significant market move, the automation automatically sends a pre-approved reassurance communication to clients explaining the context in plain language and reaffirming the plan already in place, reducing the volume of anxious inbound calls that otherwise flood the office during exactly the moment staff are already stretched thin.

The financial advisor can review which clients opened the message and flag anyone who still seems worried for a personal follow-up call, letting a single well-timed communication calm the majority of the client base while focused human attention goes to the handful of clients who genuinely need it.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, a financial advisor has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: Document Retention Compliance Sweep
automations.summary: The automation automatically flags documents that have reached the end of their required retention period, routing them for archiving or destruction…
steps: The automation automatically flags documents that have reached the end of their required retention period, routing them for archiving or destruction according to the firm's compliance policy instead of a records manager periodically combing through file storage trying to remember what's actually due for disposal.

Every flagged document goes through a review step before anything is destroyed, so nothing important is lost by mistake, and the firm gains a clean, dated log proving its retention policy is actually being followed rather than existing only as a written policy nobody consistently enforces.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, a records manager has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time.
tools: Google Sheets or Airtable (return status dashboard)

automations.title: Advisor Licensing & CE Credit Tracker
automations.summary: The automation internally tracks each advisor's required licensing and continuing education credits, alerting both the advisor and the HR and…
steps: The automation internally tracks each advisor's required licensing and continuing education credits, alerting both the advisor and the HR and licensing coordinator well before any credential is at risk of lapsing, rather than a license expiration being discovered only when a routine audit or a client transaction gets blocked by an inactive registration.

Credit progress is tracked against each state and designation's specific requirement, and advisors get a running count of exactly how many hours are still needed before the deadline, turning what used to be a stressful last-minute scramble every renewal cycle into a routine, low-drama part of the calendar.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a hr & licensing coordinator is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: Google Sheets or Airtable (return status dashboard)

automations.title: Account Aggregation Sync Failure Alert
automations.summary: The automation automatically flags when a client's linked outside account data hasn't refreshed in a while, prompting a follow-up so the wealth…
steps: The automation automatically flags when a client's linked outside account data hasn't refreshed in a while, prompting a follow-up so the wealth management associate is always working from current numbers instead of unknowingly building a recommendation on stale balances that stopped syncing weeks earlier.

A silently broken account link used to only get caught when a client questioned a number that didn't match their own statement, and catching the sync failure proactively instead means every conversation is grounded in data that's actually current.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, a wealth management associate has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: New Regulation Training Assignment Automation
automations.summary: When a new compliance regulation is identified, the automation automatically assigns the required training module to relevant staff with a tracked…
steps: When a new compliance regulation is identified, the automation automatically assigns the required training module to relevant staff with a tracked completion deadline, instead of the compliance officer manually identifying who needs the training and chasing down completion one person at a time.

Staff who haven't completed the assigned training as the deadline approaches are automatically flagged for a reminder, and the firm gains a clean, dated record proving every relevant employee was actually trained on a regulatory change, exactly the kind of documentation that matters most during an examination.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means a compliance officer re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
tools: Google Sheets or Airtable (return status dashboard)

automations.title: Client Meeting Prep Packet Automation
automations.summary: Ahead of a scheduled client meeting, the automation automatically compiles a prep packet, an account summary, a suggested agenda, any open items…
steps: Ahead of a scheduled client meeting, the automation automatically compiles a prep packet, an account summary, a suggested agenda, any open items from the last touchpoint, so the financial advisor walks in fully prepared instead of pulling account data and reconstructing open items from memory in the ten minutes before the meeting starts.

Every meeting starts from a consistent, complete picture regardless of how busy the week has been, and clients notice the difference when their advisor clearly already knows exactly where things stand instead of needing the client to catch them up first.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, a financial advisor has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
tools: Google Sheets or Airtable (return status dashboard)

automations.title: Tax Document Delivery Confirmation & Reminder
automations.summary: The automation tracks whether a client has actually downloaded or received their tax documents and automatically sends a reminder if they remain…
steps: The automation tracks whether a client has actually downloaded or received their tax documents and automatically sends a reminder if they remain unopened as the filing deadline approaches, instead of the tax manager assuming a document was received simply because it was sent.

Clients who never noticed the original delivery email get a second chance to actually see it before the deadline creates real pressure, and the volume of last-minute "I never got my documents" calls the week before filing drops sharply once delivery confirmation, not just sending, is what the firm actually tracks.
automations.manualProcess: Without a system in place, a tax manager has to manually chase down updates, send reminders one by one, and hope nothing falls through the cracks.
tools: Client portal (e.g., TaxDome, Canopy, or Karbon)

automations.title: Service Tier Review Automation
automations.summary: The automation periodically reviews client accounts against service tier criteria, assets under management, engagement complexity, and flags…
steps: The automation periodically reviews client accounts against service tier criteria, assets under management, engagement complexity, and flags candidates for a tier upgrade or a review conversation, instead of the practice manager relying on someone remembering to periodically audit the client list by hand.

Clients who've genuinely outgrown their current tier get identified automatically instead of quietly staying underserved or underpriced for years, and the firm captures revenue and service alignment opportunities that a purely manual review process would routinely miss.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, a practice manager has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: Google Sheets or Airtable (return status dashboard)

automations.title: Advisor Book-of-Business Handoff Workflow
automations.summary: When an advisor transitions roles or leaves the firm, the automation automatically triggers the client handoff communication and reassignment…
steps: When an advisor transitions roles or leaves the firm, the automation automatically triggers the client handoff communication and reassignment workflow to the new advisor, instead of the operations manager manually reassigning dozens or hundreds of client relationships one at a time while also drafting individual transition letters.

Every affected client automatically receives a warm, professional introduction to their new advisor at the same time the internal reassignment happens, and a transition that used to take weeks and risk client attrition along the way now happens smoothly within days.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, an operations manager has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time.

automations.title: Claim-Type Document Checklist Automation
automations.summary: Once a claim is opened, the client automatically receives the specific document checklist required for that claim type, reducing the back-and-forth…
steps: Once a claim is opened, the client automatically receives the specific document checklist required for that claim type, reducing the back-and-forth over what's needed that used to require the claims coordinator to explain the requirements verbally and often repeat the explanation when a client forgot half of it.

Every claim type has its own pre-built, accurate checklist rather than a generic one that leaves clients guessing, and claims move through the process faster once clients know exactly what to gather from the very first message instead of learning it piece by piece over several calls.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on a claims coordinator, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving.
tools: Karbon or a practice management system

automations.title: Post-Life-Event Check-In Survey
automations.summary: After a major transaction such as a home purchase, a retirement, or an inheritance, the client automatically receives a check-in survey designed to…
steps: After a major transaction such as a home purchase, a retirement, or an inheritance, the client automatically receives a check-in survey designed to surface additional service needs that a financial advisor might not otherwise hear about until months later in casual conversation.

A new inheritance often means a need for updated estate planning, a home purchase often means a need for updated insurance, and catching that need right after the life event happens, while it's genuinely top of mind for the client, turns a routine check-in into a natural, well-timed service conversation.
automations.manualProcess: Left unautomated, a financial advisor spends hours on the parts of this job that don't require judgment: copying data, sending reminders, and tracking status by hand. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Annual Fee Disclosure Renewal Automation
automations.summary: Required annual fee and conflict-of-interest disclosures are automatically generated and sent to every client each year for acknowledgment, keeping…
steps: Required annual fee and conflict-of-interest disclosures are automatically generated and sent to every client each year for acknowledgment, keeping the firm compliant without the compliance officer manually tracking which clients have and haven't acknowledged the current year's disclosure.

Clients who haven't acknowledged within a reasonable window automatically receive a reminder, and the firm always has a clean, complete, dated record of compliance across the entire client base instead of a partial one that only reflects whichever clients happened to respond to the first request.
automations.manualProcess: Without a system in place, a compliance officer has to manually chase down updates, send reminders one by one, and hope nothing falls through the cracks.

automations.title: Client Complaint Escalation Workflow
automations.summary: A logged client complaint automatically triggers a defined escalation workflow, notifying compliance immediately and setting a tracked resolution…
steps: A logged client complaint automatically triggers a defined escalation workflow, notifying compliance immediately and setting a tracked resolution deadline, so nothing falls through the cracks the way an informally handled complaint sometimes does when it's addressed verbally and never actually documented anywhere.

Every complaint follows the same consistent process regardless of who first received it, and the compliance officer has a complete, timestamped record showing exactly how and when each complaint was resolved, precisely the kind of documentation regulators expect a firm to be able to produce on request.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on a compliance officer remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.
tools: Google Sheets or Airtable (return status dashboard)
